pages.lesson:
LESSON: READING 2.4.1 INTENSIVE READING: CLASS READER

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 2
Topic 2.4: Reading 2.4.1 Intensive Reading: Class Reader

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Reading 2.4.1 Intensive Reading: Class Reader. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why should we not judge a book by its cover?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. explain the different parts that aid in previewing a book
2. describe the author and the setting of the text in terms of time and place

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: READING 2.4.1 INTENSIVE READING: CLASS READER
Subject: ENGLISH · Grade: Grade 7
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Reading 2.4.1 Intensive Reading: Class Reader helps you succeed in ENGLISH. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: READING 2.4.1 INTENSIVE READING: CLASS READER
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Explain the different parts that aid in previewing a book

What this means
In this part you learn to explain the different parts that aid in previewing a book. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: explain the different parts that aid in previewing a book.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 2.4.1 Intensive Reading: Class Reader”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can explain the different parts that aid in previewing a book. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Describe the author and the setting of the text in terms of time and place

What this means
In this part you learn to describe the author and the setting of the text in terms of time and place. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: describe the author and the setting of the text in terms of time and place.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading 2.4.1 Intensive Reading: Class Reader to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can describe the author and the setting of the text in terms of time and place. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Reading 2.4.1 Intensive Reading: Class Reader is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 2.4.1 Intensive Reading: Class Reader”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: explain the different parts that aid in previewing a book)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading 2.4.1 Intensive Reading: Class Reader to a partner. (skill: describe the author and the setting of the text in terms of time and place)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Reading 2.4.1 Intensive Reading: Class Reader to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: explain the different parts that aid in previewing a book.
3. Practise this skill: describe the author and the setting of the text in terms of time and place.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Reading 2.4.1 Intensive Reading: Class Reader from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Reading 2.4.1 Intensive Reading: Class Reader: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 7 learner study Reading 2.4.1 Intensive Reading: Class Reader?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why should we not judge a book by its cover?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Reading 2.4.1 Intensive Reading: Class Reader means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: explain the different parts that aid in previewing a book.
5. Be able to: describe the author and the setting of the text in terms of time and place.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
